column8: 1. Periodic education or training on infection prevention and control is conducted in my department.
column9: 2. Infection control guidelines are available and accessible in my department.
column10: 3. Hospital-acquired infections can be transmitted through contaminated medical equipment.
column11: 4. Nosocomial infection refers to an infection acquired during hospital stay rather than from home.
column12: 5. I wash my hands before and after every direct contact with patients.
column13: 6. I am aware of the WHO Five Moments of Hand Hygiene.
column14: 7. All healthcare workers and patients should be considered potentially infectious.
column15: 8. Clean water alone is sufficient to destroy harmful microorganisms.
column16: 9. Body fluids should never be handled with bare hands, even if gloves are unavailable.
column17: 10. I have adequate knowledge regarding prevention and control of hospital-acquired infections.
column18: 11. Personal protective equipment (PPE) is always available when needed in my department.
column19: 12. I wear masks and eye protection during invasive or high-risk procedures.
column20: 13. I attend in-service training or workshops related to infection prevention and control at least once a year.
column21: 14. I wear appropriate PPE when handling contaminated linen or hospital waste.
column22: 15. Proper infection prevention and control practices improve patient outcomes.
